newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MOVES PLANNED TO EASE PREMIER LEAGUE FIXTURE CHAOS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOVES PLANNED TO EASE PREMIER LEAGUE FIXTURE CHAOS.

text.p: The new head of English soccer's premier league said on Wednesday he would propose moves to end the fixture congestion which clubs such as Manchester United face.
Premier league chief executive Peter Leaver wants the power to redraw the fixture list to suit circumstances and the right to order clubs to play on specific dates.

The premier league angered Manchester United earlier this month when it refused the champions' request for the season to be extended. That left United having to play four matches in eight days to complete their fixtures by the May 11 deadline.

Leaver told delegates at the SoccerEx conference that there was no provision under current premier league rules to amend the fixture list drawn up at the start of the season. Postponed games have to be slotted into the calendar wherever there is room.
Arsenal vice-chairman David Dein said his club would like to reduce the number of games played by opting out of the League Cup.
"As far as Arsenal are concerned, we'd rather not go in for it," he said.

Leading clubs like Arsenal and Manchester United contend that a 20-club premier league is simply too large. But all the other members oppose a reduction, fearing lost income from fewer games or exclusion from a smaller elite.
Dein said he believed European soccer's ruling body UEFA would one day insist on a maximum of 18 clubs in top divisions.
"I think UEFA will ultimately make it a condition of entry into their competitions," he said.
